raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Trainers look up token-space strategies with `strategy_for`, but only `import_processors` registered them, and it lives in `managers/multimodal_processor.py`, which imports the serving stack (`BaseMultimodalProcessor`, the token-space wrapper, `ServerArgs`). A trainer therefore found no strategy for any architecture.

## Modifications

- `registry.register_token_space_models()`: imports every `token_space_mm_process.models` module and registers its strategies and serving specs; a module that fails to import is skipped with a warning. `registry.py` still imports no model module itself.
- The four multimodal serving entry points (tokenizer manager, scheduler, encoder receiver, Rust server) call it instead of `import_processors` on the models package, behind their existing multimodal checks; `import_processors` registers only legacy processors again.

## Tests

- `test_processor_trainer_import.py`: a fresh process that forbids serving imports registers strategies and gets the Qwen strategy from `strategy_for`.
- `test_token_space_registry.py`: importing the manager still loads no strategy module; a broken model module is skipped.

## Stack

Based on #47344, as a follow-up to the MM refactor stack (#43420, #46408 - #46415).

+"""Compare the original and refactored Qwen async processor boundaries bit for bit.
+
+    pinned benchmark rows + rendered prompts + SHA-256 checked local media
+                     |                         |
+        legacy route subprocess        candidate route subprocess
+        full input_text every turn     input_ids; expanded prefix + new suffix
+                     |                         |
+        legacy Qwen class          serving factory -> Qwen token-space processor
+                     |                         |
+        process_mm_data_async      process_mm_data_async
+                     |                         |
+           final IDs + every output/item field + tensor shape/dtype/raw bytes
+                     +---------- exact comparison ----------+
+
+The same Python environment and checkpoint processor files serve both captures.
+Every turn supplies its full ordered media URL lists without session recipes.
+All output fields are compared unchanged, including item grouping, offsets and
+mRoPE, except the cache identity (item hash / pad value, padded IDs), which the
+routes derive differently.
+Legacy resizes Qwen3-VL family videos with the Qwen2-VL factor, so its capture
+preprocesses them as the token-space route does (pinned to qwen-vl-utils elsewhere).
+No model weights or generation are needed. CUDA CI runs a small pinned matrix
+through both real routes: Qwen3.5 and Qwen2.5-VL with two images, Qwen3-VL with
+an image then a video, Qwen3-Omni with an image then one audio clip; one backend
+per model covers PIL and the GPU path.
+Turns are joined at an explicit assistant end token.
+Both routes run from the same clean checkout; only the candidate enables the
+startup strategy.

+def _snapshot(value):
+    if isinstance(value, torch.Tensor):
+        tensor = value.detach().cpu().contiguous()
+        return {
+            "type": "torch.Tensor",
+            "shape": tuple(tensor.shape),
+            "dtype": str(tensor.dtype),
+            "bytes": tensor.reshape(-1).view(torch.uint8).numpy().tobytes(),
+        }
+    if isinstance(value, np.ndarray):
+        return {
+            "type": "numpy.ndarray",
+            "shape": value.shape,
+            "dtype": value.dtype.str,
+            "bytes": value.tobytes(order="C"),
+        }
+    if isinstance(value, msgspec.Struct):
+        return _snapshot(msgspec.structs.asdict(value))
+    if isinstance(value, Enum):
+        return (type(value).__name__, value.name)
+    if isinstance(value, dict):
+        return {key: _snapshot(item) for key, item in value.items()}
+    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
+        return type(value)(_snapshot(item) for item in value)
+    if isinstance(value, np.generic):
+        return ("numpy.scalar", value.dtype.str, value.tobytes())
+    if isinstance(value, float):
+        return ("float64", struct.pack("!d", value))
+    if value is None or isinstance(value, (bool, int, str, bytes)):
+        return value
+    raise TypeError(f"Uncaptured processor output type: {type(value).__qualname__}")

+# Cache identity: legacy keys it by artifact or by feature bytes, token space by
+# feature bytes scoped by the item's grids, so the routes never compare it.
+_CACHE_IDENTITY_ITEM_FIELDS = ("hash", "pad_value", "pad_values", "identity")

+def _drop_cache_identity(reference_cases, candidate_cases):
+    for case_id in reference_cases.keys() & candidate_cases.keys():
+        sides = [
+            cases[case_id].get("model_inputs")
+            for cases in (reference_cases, candidate_cases)
+            if isinstance(cases[case_id], dict)
+        ]
+        if len(sides) != 2 or None in sides:
+            continue
+        for side in sides:
+            side.pop("padded_input_ids", None)
+            for item in side.get("mm_items") or []:
+                for name in _CACHE_IDENTITY_ITEM_FIELDS:
+                    item.pop(name, None)

+def _assert_identical(reference, candidate, field="output"):
+    assert type(reference) is type(candidate), f"{field}: types differ"
+    if isinstance(reference, dict):
+        assert reference.keys() == candidate.keys(), (
+            f"{field}: fields differ: "
+            f"reference-only={reference.keys() - candidate.keys()}, "
+            f"candidate-only={candidate.keys() - reference.keys()}"
+        )
+        for key in reference:
+            _assert_identical(reference[key], candidate[key], f"{field}.{key}")
+    elif isinstance(reference, (list, tuple)):
+        assert len(reference) == len(candidate), f"{field}: lengths differ"
+        for index, (old, new) in enumerate(zip(reference, candidate)):
+            _assert_identical(old, new, f"{field}[{index}]")
+    elif isinstance(reference, bytes):
+        assert reference == candidate, f"{field}: raw bytes differ"
+    else:
+        assert reference == candidate, f"{field}: {reference!r} != {candidate!r}"

+def _sha256(path):
+    with Path(path).open("rb") as stream:
+        return hashlib.file_digest(stream, "sha256").hexdigest()

+def _checkpoint_files(checkpoint):
+    weight_suffixes = {".safetensors", ".bin", ".pt", ".pth", ".onnx", ".gguf"}
+    return {
+        str(path.relative_to(checkpoint)): _sha256(path)
+        for path in sorted(checkpoint.rglob("*"))
+        if path.is_file()
+        and path.suffix not in weight_suffixes
+        and ".cache" not in path.parts
+        and ".git" not in path.parts
+    }

+def _make_hf_processor(processor_class, patch_size, *, model_type="qwen3_vl"):
+    # This tokenizer has a real noncanonical sequence: [D, escribe] decodes to
+    # Describe, whose canonical encoding is one token.
+    tokens = ["[UNK]", "[PAD]", "Describe", "D", "escribe"] + [
+        f"unused_{i}" for i in range(5, EOS + 1)
+    ]
+    for token_id, text in TOKEN_TEXT.items():
+        tokens[token_id] = text
+    tokens.extend([f"<{tenth / 10:.1f}" for tenth in range(100)] + ["seconds>"])
+    vocab = {text: token_id for token_id, text in enumerate(tokens)}
+    backend = Tokenizer(models.WordLevel(vocab, unk_token="[UNK]"))
+    backend.pre_tokenizer = pre_tokenizers.WhitespaceSplit()
+    backend.decoder = decoders.Fuse()
+    tokenizer = PreTrainedTokenizerFast(
+        tokenizer_object=backend,
+        unk_token="[UNK]",
+        pad_token="[PAD]",

+            "audio_bos_token": "<|vision_start|>",
+            "audio_eos_token": "<|vision_end|>",

+    _attach_core(

+        QwenTokenSpaceProcessStrategy(
+            _component_config(processor), processor._processor
+        ),
+    )
